audit_notes: Model: steady transport of diatom cells across a near-wall transport layer of thickness delta (normalised coordinate y, wall at y=0, outer edge at y=1), d2c/dy2 = 0, with a first-order wall reaction at y=0 whose effective attachment velocity is the contact attachment velocity times the fraction of attached cells that survive the service wall shear, exp(-tau_w/tau_adh). The net retained settlement flux is J = (D/delta) dc/dy(0) = k_eff c_b/(1 + Da), Da = delta k_eff/D. Design (tau_adh = 12 Pa): k_eff = 1e-4*exp(-25/12) = 1.25e-5 m/s, Da = 0.062, J = 1.17e4 cells/(m^2 s). Baseline silicone foul-release (tau_adh = 30 Pa): k_eff = 4.35e-5 m/s, Da = 0.217, J = 3.57e4 cells/(m^2 s). Expected gain: 67 % lower net retained settlement flux. Caveats: (1) the exponential survival law is an assumption standing in for a distribution of adhesion strengths; (2) the result depends almost entirely on the ratio of adhesion strengths (12 vs 30 Pa), which is taken from short-term lab flow-cell data on fresh amphiphilic surfaces and may not persist in service; (3) ships spend 10-40 % of time idle at zero shear, when the survival factor is 1 for both coatings and the benefit vanishes, so the time-averaged benefit on slime accumulation is smaller; (4) the model does not compute drag. Dimensionless numbers: Damkoehler number of the wall reaction 0.062 (design) and 0.217 (baseline), i.e. reaction-limited, so the adhesion ratio controls the flux; shear-to-adhesion ratio 2.08 (design) vs 0.83 (baseline). Near-wall Reynolds number of a 10 um cell, u_tau*d/nu = 0.16*1e-5/1e-6 = 1.6. Parameter check: all positive; wall shear 25 Pa corresponds to u_tau = sqrt(25/1025) = 0.156 m/s, consistent with a hull at about 12 kn; hydration layer thickness, biofilm thickness and biofilm viscosity are not used in this model (informational). Stress check: no structural load; the zwitterionic surface layer must survive abrasion and hydrolysis, a durability risk not a simulation failure. The simulation coefficient is the design effective attachment velocity k_eff = 1.25e-5 m/s (informational).
